I farm wheat and maize on the same 9.5 mu in rotation, so I will put the full 9.5 mu into winter wheat first and then summer maize after wheat harvest. I have 30 years of experience, well irrigation, and a family with some off-farm work, so I will keep the plan steady and practical rather than take risks. For wheat, I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer at a moderate-to-strong level, irrigate a few key times, and use rotary tillage because it fits my scale and saves labor. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because yield matters most to me in maize, keep nitrogen a bit higher than wheat, give fewer irrigations because of the season, and keep pesticide sprays limited to what is needed. I will aim for stable output and manageable labor, not the most aggressive input plan.
